summary: Edward Sapir was a linguist who studied at Columbia University under Wilhelm Wundt and Franz Boas. He served at the Geological Survey of Canada (circa 1910–1925), the University of Chicago (circa 1925–1931), and Yale University (circa 1931–1939).
Edward Upham worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society and a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London.

Edward Vernon Arnold was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Cambridge and the University of Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He was a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge, and served as professor at Bangor University (1884–1924).

Edward Washburn Hopkins was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Columbia and Leipzig under Ernst Windisch and Albrecht Weber. He taught at Columbia, served as professor at Bryn Mawr (1885–1895), and was professor at Yale (1895–1926).

Edward Winslow Bastian works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Geshe Lobsang Tenzin, Geshe Lobsang, and Geshe Lobsang Donyo, and was a research scholar at Banaras.

Edwin Arnold was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who studied at King's College London and the University of Oxford. He served as Principal of Deccan College (1856) and visiting lecturer at Keio University.

Edwin F. Bryant is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed his doctorate at Columbia University in 1997. He taught at Harvard University (circa 1997–2002) and became Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University circa 2003.

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar who studied at Trinity College Dublin. He served as President of The Asiatic Society (1886–1887) and Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (circa 1888–1890).

Edwin Gerow is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen, Louis Renou, George V. Bobrinskoy, and V. Ranganathan. He held posts at the University of Washington (circa 1966–1978) and Reed College (circa 1978–2003).

Edwin Norris worked in linguistics, history, archaeology, and Indology. He was employed by the East India Company (1818–1837), the Foreign Office (1847–1866), and held multiple secretarial and librarian posts at the Royal Asiatic Society between 1836 and 1861.

Edwin Whitfield Fay was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Rhodes College, Johns Hopkins, and Leipzig. He held teaching posts at Michigan, Washington and Lee (1893–1899), and served as professor of Latin at the University of Texas at Austin.

Egaku Maeda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno. He held professorships at Tokai Gakuen, Meijo, and Aichi Gakuin University (1972–2002).

Eido Tai Shimano was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher who studied at Ryutaku-ji and the University of Hawaiʻi under Soen Nakagawa. He served as abbot at the Zen Studies Society and shika at New York Zendo Shobo-ji and Dai Bosatsu Zendo Kongo-ji.

Eiichi Makino was a scholar of law and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (circa 1903–1938), Chuo University (circa 1904–1938), Shiraume Gakuen Junior College, Kyushu University, and Tohoku University.
Eiichi Yamaguchi is an Indologist and philosopher. He completed graduate studies at Kyushu University (attested 1986–1990) and served there as a research assistant (attested 1990–1991).

Eiki Hoshino is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University (circa 1962–1966). He served at Taisho University as Professor in the Faculty of Humanities and Director (circa 1980–2013).

Eileen Power was a historian who studied at Girton College, Cambridge, and the University of Paris. She held posts at the University of London and the London School of Economics from circa 1921 to 1940.

Eisaku Okada is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Kyoto University. He has held positions as a JSPS research fellow, Koyasan University researcher, and Kyoto University part-time lecturer (attested 2014–2015).
Eisei Kojima was a scholar of Buddhist studies. In 1976, he is attested as serving as a professor at Ryukoku University and as president of Doho University.
Eishu Miyazaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University under Gyoo Kageyama. He held posts at Minobusan University and Rissho University (circa 1949–1984).
